messages:
dina: Heads up — Acme escalated: streaming requests to /v1/streams intermittently show 'broken pipe' on the gateway and are being recorded as 5xx in billing. Customer is seeing unexpected charges.

ben: link to trace? request ids? short repro?

dina: trace: https://console.redwood/trace/trace-9b7c
request-ids: req_20260317_01, req_20260317_04, req_20260317_07
curl repro:
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams -d '{"prompt":"...","stream":true}'
```
client-side shows `write failed: broken pipe` after ~5s of tokens

cory: which runtime? hosted? region?

dina: hosted / us-east-1. Model: gpt-open-13b-8k-quant. SDK: node-fetch 3.3.0 inside electron app (customer says chrome extension)

elaine: can you paste gateway logs for these req ids (gateway request_id, upstream status, bytes_sent)?

dina: paste logs:
```
[2026-03-17T15:12:03Z] req=req_20260317_01 gateway: upstream write failed: EPIPE, bytes_sent=1024, upstream_status=200
[2026-03-17T15:12:08Z] req=req_20260317_04 gateway: client disconnected during response, bytes_sent=2048, downstream_err=broken pipe, classify=5xx
[2026-03-17T15:12:12Z] req=req_20260317_07 gateway: upstream closed first, bytes_sent=0, classify=5xx
```

ops-bot: alert: streaming-early-eof-rate spike +350% in us-east-1 between 15:00-15:30

ben: ok. current billing heuristic treats any aborted streaming connection with bytes_sent < min_threshold as 5xx. That is too blunt. Need to distinguish downstream (client) abort vs upstream/gateway error.

cory: quick check — bytes_sent > 0 and downstream err 'broken pipe' likely client closed. If upstream_status==200 and upstream didn't return error then it shouldn't be billed as 5xx. We'll need to inspect tcp reset flags from proxy logs.

elaine: assigned eng-runtime @cory to investigate. action: (1) reproduce with chrome extension that does mid-stream cancel (2) confirm gateway logs have FIN from client vs RST from upstream (3) patch classification to classify client FIN as client_abort (not 5xx)

cory: I can reproduce with a small node script that pipes then force-close socket. repro steps attached.

cory: node repro snippet:
```
const req = fetch(url, opts);
setTimeout(() => req.body.cancel(), 3000);
```
observed gateway log: downstream FIN, bytes_sent ~1200, upstream status 200

dina: customer says they cancel the stream when they get desired partial output. They think we're billing incorrectly.

ben: let's hold billing for those req ids pending classification fix. Support: create ticket with billing team for tentative refund scope: customer tenant id ACME-123, affected reqs listed.

elaine: eng-runtime plan: patch heuristics to count downstream_FIN with bytes_sent>0 as client_abort, deploy canary to us-east-1, monitor for false-negatives. roll timeline: patch today, canary by EOD, rollout tomorrow.

cory: I'll open PR and include log parsing for tcp flags and bytes_sent thresholds. link: https://github.com/redwood/eng-runtime/pull/452

dina: customer update prepared: "we're investigating and suspect client-side cancels are being misclassified; holding billing while we fix" :thumbsup:

ops-bot: incident updated: INC-2026-0317-13 status=investigating owner=@cory

ben: follow-ups: add testcases to e2e streaming suite, update docs about client cancel semantics, add metric to track client_abort vs gateway_error ratio.

elaine: assigning billing ticket to @ben for refund decision after eng triage

dina: thanks team. will ping when PR merged and billing decision made

cory: PR merged to canary at 17:40, will monitor. logs look good so far — client_abort counts trending up, 5xx counts down.

dina: customer confirmed they see updated billing hold. closing for now, reopen if we see regression. :white_check_mark:
